about: Named combinations. These outrank single placements in the reading, so the engine shows them first.

rules.name: Gajakesari yoga
rules.says: Jupiter stands in an angle from the Moon: judgement and feeling work together, which shows up as steadiness under pressure and a reputation that survives setbacks.

rules.name: Budha-Aditya yoga
rules.says: The Sun and Mercury together put intelligence at the centre of the identity: articulate, quick to read a situation, and usually recognised for it.
rules.note: Retired on review: the reading was judged wrong and the engine no longer evaluates it. Kept rather than deleted so the id stays resolvable - yog.budha-aditya.burnt named it in conflictsWith, and a reading saved before this date still refers to it. Note that nothing else in the base now speaks to the Sun and Mercury sharing a house unless Mercury is burnt, so a chart where Mercury is clear of the Sun says nothing about the pair at all.

rules.name: Budha-Aditya with Mercury combust
rules.says: Mercury is close enough to the Sun to be burnt, and a substantial line of authority holds that this cancels Budha-Aditya outright rather than merely weakening it: the intelligence is there, but it is not recognised, and speaking at the wrong moment costs more than staying quiet would have.

sources.locus: on the avasthas of the grahas and combustion
on the Sun and Mercury together

rules.note: Mercury shares the Sun's sign in about half of all charts and is burnt in roughly two thirds of those, so this reading reaches around a third of charts. It was marked disputed while the opposing yog.budha-aditya stood against it; that rule was retired on review, so this is no longer one side of an argument and is stated plainly.

rules.name: Chandra-Mangala yoga
rules.says: The Moon with Mars gives drive to earn and a willingness to act on feeling; money comes readily and so does friction at home.

rules.name: Kuja (Mangal) dosha
rules.says: Mars occupies one of the five houses that classically strain marriage. Traditionally read as a warning about temper and timing in partnership, not as a verdict on it.
rules.note: Which houses count is genuinely disputed: some traditions include the 2nd, some exclude the 1st, and most hold the dosha cancelled when both charts carry it or when Mars is in its own or exaltation sign. AstroBot reports it and does not act on it.

rules.name: Ruchaka yoga
rules.says: Mars is dignified and placed in an angle: physical confidence, command in a crisis, and a body that holds up to being used.

rules.name: Bhadra yoga
rules.says: Mercury is dignified in an angle: unusual clarity of expression, and a mind that gets trusted with decisions belonging to other people.

rules.name: Hamsa yoga
rules.says: Jupiter is dignified in an angle: moral authority that others defer to without being asked, and good fortune that looks like good character.

rules.name: Malavya yoga
rules.says: Venus is dignified in an angle: comfort, attractiveness and the means to enjoy both, with taste that other people borrow.

rules.name: Sasa yoga
rules.says: Saturn is dignified in an angle: durable authority built slowly, with a capacity for work that wears down opposition.

rules.name: Sunapha yoga
rules.says: A planet stands in the second from the Moon: resources gather through effort rather than arriving unasked.

rules.name: Anapha yoga
rules.says: A planet stands in the twelfth from the Moon: well-formed physically and inclined to spend on others, with a late turn towards letting things go.

rules.name: Durudhara yoga
rules.says: The Moon is flanked on both sides: support arrives from more than one direction, and little has to be done entirely alone.

rules.name: Kemadruma yoga
rules.says: The Moon stands unsupported on either side: a tendency to carry things alone, and stretches where help is genuinely absent.
rules.note: Classically cancelled when a planet sits in an angle from the Moon or from the Lagna. Check Gajakesari and the kendra placements before giving this any weight.

rules.name: Adhi yoga
rules.says: Benefics gather in the sixth, seventh and eighth from the Moon: a settled life with real standing, arrived at without much drama.

rules.name: Shakata yoga
rules.says: The Moon falls in the sixth or eighth from Jupiter: fortune arrives in cycles, and what was gained has a way of needing to be rebuilt.
rules.note: Many practitioners consider this yoga overstated and set it aside when the chart is otherwise strong.

rules.name: Amala yoga
rules.says: A benefic occupies the tenth from the Moon or the Lagna: a clean reputation that holds, and work others speak well of.

rules.name: Vesi yoga
rules.says: A planet stands in the second from the Sun: speaks plainly and is believed, with a directness that reads as honesty or as bluntness depending on the room.

rules.name: Vasi yoga
rules.says: A planet stands in the twelfth from the Sun: generous, well regarded, and inclined to act through others rather than directly.

rules.name: Kala Sarpa yoga
rules.says: All seven grahas fall on one side of the Rahu-Ketu axis: life tends to run in a single strong current, with long waits followed by abrupt movement.
rules.note: Not found in BPHS, Phaladeepika or Saravali. A comparatively recent construction, popular in practice and treated sceptically by many classicists. Weighted low for that reason.

rules.name: Parivartana between the Lagna and the 10th
rules.says: The lords of the first and tenth exchange houses: identity and work are bound together, so the career is rarely experienced as merely a job.

rules.name: Parivartana between the 2nd and 11th
rules.says: The lords of the second and eleventh exchange houses: income converts into holdings efficiently, which is the plainest wealth signature in the system.

rules.name: Parivartana between the 5th and 9th
rules.says: The two trine lords exchange houses: merit and fortune reinforce each other, usually through a teacher or a line of learning.
